Vanessa / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — HealthSync leadership liked the latency profile and the observability features. We need a few clarifications to move procurement along:

- Can you confirm how the platform fee vs node (GPU) licensing breaks down for a 3-site VPC pilot (US-west, US-east, EU-west)?
- We asked about an "integration rollback credit" in case the migration blocks our go-live and we have to revert to the incumbent for up to 60 days. Is that something Redwood will entertain and how would it be capped?
- SRE on-call: the internal expectation here is a 24x7 escalation window for severity-1s during the pilot, plus two named on-call backups. Would that be part of the support tiers or an add-on?

I've attached our requirements doc. Procurement is looped on this thread so they can confirm procurement windows and PO cadence.

Thanks,

Maria — really appreciate the quick note and the clear asks. High-level reply inline below; internal folks copied to lock down numbers and legal/finance constraints.

- Platform fee vs node licensing: for a 3-site pilot we typically propose a time-limited platform fee + metered node SKUs. Example: $75k/mo platform fee (includes control plane, telemetry retention SLOs for pilot) + $X/hour per GPU node (we'll compute per-region node counts in the proposal). We can propose a blended pilot rate that caps monthly spend.

- Rollback credit: we can offer a limited "rollback credit" tied to integration work we perform that directly causes rollback (e.g., migration scripts, operator changes). Suggested structure: up to 30% of the pilot platform fee (cap $22.5k) credit applied if you revert within the first 60 days and the root cause is traced to integration produced by Redwood. This credit is intended to reduce your risk and is conditional on a joint RCA. I'll ask legal to draft language.

- SRE on-call: 24x7 escalation during pilot is considered an elevated support band. For pilots we typically include a "pilot on-call" add-on: named on-call + two backups, 2-hour response for Sev1s, and 8/5 for Sev2. Cost for the pilot on-call add-on is typically monthly; Marissa / David — please propose a pilot on-call fee (and a replacement pricing option if they want it included in the platform fee).

I'll attach a quick price worksheet and a draft of the rollback terms. Maria — would you prefer a DocuSign envelope or a redlined PDF?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Maria — a couple of technical clarifications that affect commercial: 

1) Scope for rollback credit: from a technical standpoint we should enumerate what counts as "integration work by Redwood" — my recommendation: migration orchestration playbooks, Helm/operator patches, infra-as-code templates, and model-serving config changes that we author. Client-side config or third-party infra changes wouldn't qualify.

2) SRE on-call scope: if HealthSync needs 24x7 coverage with a 2-hour initial response and playbook-driven incident handling, that requires a named SRE team and a runbook. For the pilot we can commit to a reduced headcount model (1 primary + 2 backups) and include up to 20 hours/month of remediation work; additional breakfix hours billed at hourly rates or pulled from an agreed remediation credit.

3) Integration credits: we can offer an "engineering credit" of 40 hours to cover migration-specific work (testing, preflight checks, scripted rollback) as part of the pilot discount. If more hours are needed, we invoice at SOW rates.

I'll add these bullets to the migration_rollback_terms.docx for legal.

— Markus
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Team — quick finance/legal note on the commercial constructs Vanessa suggested:

- Platform fee: for a pilot we can discount the standard platform fee by 20% if HealthSync commits to a 12-month renewal on conversion. If they decline a conversion commitment we can still offer a one-time pilot blended cap.
- Rollback credit: negotiated credit needs to be symmetrical and tied to an RCA; legal will limit the credit to direct fees (platform fee and migration engineering) and exclude consequential damages. Proposed cap: $25k or 30% of pilot platform fee, whichever is lower.
- SRE on-call: recommend we present two options to the customer: (A) included in pilot at an incremental flat fee of $18k/mo (named SREs + 20 hours remediation included) or (B) pay-as-you-go with a 100-hour remediation credit at a reduced hourly rate.

I'll prepare a short commercial summary and a DocuSign envelope for the pilot MSA + rollback addendum. Marissa — can you confirm list pricing for the node SKUs so I can build the blended cap?

David Kim
Director, Finance | Redwood Inference
